newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says seriously concerned about Belarus poll.
newsitem.headline: EU says seriously concerned about Belarus poll.

text.p: The European Union said on Thursday it was still seriously concerned about events in Belarus and urged that last Sunday's referendum on presidential powers be considered consultative, not binding.
"The European Union remains seriously concerned at the situation in Belarus, and particularly the issue of the constitutional referendum," the European Union said in a statement released on Tuesday.
Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko announced a crushing victory after Sunday's referendum to widen his powers and extend his term in office by two years.
Opponents such as the Belarus parliamentary speaker, Semyon Sharetsky, described the outcome as a "farce" which would lead to dictatorship in the former Soviet republic.

"The European Union is particulalry concerned, in this regard, that the ruling of the constitutional court concerning the consultative nature of the referendum should be respected," the EU statement added.
An agreement secured last Friday between Lukashenko and opposition deputies held that the poll would be non-binding.

But Lukashenko threw out the Russian-brokered deal on Saturday, saying that neither parliament nor the constitutional court had met their half of it, a move which prompted opponents to renew their challenges to the legitimacy of the referendum in the constitutional court.

"President Lukashenko has indicated to parliament that, notwithstanding the ruling of the constitutional court, he intends to consider (the poll) result binding. The European Union deeply regrets this development.
"It urges President Lukashenko in the strongest possible terms to respect the ruling of the consitutional court," it added.
